facts.text: Ste. Marie, Illinois sits on the Embarras River in Jasper County, a spot once chosen by French settlers for its proximity to Vincennes.
Two Illinois communities share the name Sainte Marie—one in Jasper County and another in Cook County—highlighting the name’s regional popularity.
In 1837, five French brothers and relatives founded the village, signing a contract to acquire land and build a new community in eastern Illinois.
Joseph Picquet, a 19‑year‑old French explorer, was sent to the United States in 1835 to scout land for his family’s future colony.
Father Stephen Theodore Badin, the first Catholic priest ordained in the United States, blessed the new settlers’ work and celebrated Mass in their honor.
Anyone planning a building project in Ste. Marie must first obtain authorization from the village hall or Jasper County authorities.
